name: AgentScope
description: Multi-agent framework emphasizing agent teams and leader/worker coordination, planning, and human-agent interaction, with a visual multi-agent platform.
gotchas: Official repository README confirms Apache-2.0 license and describes agent teams, coordination, and planning as core capabilities

name: Agno
description: Lightweight open-source framework and runtime for building agents, teams, and workflows for production agentic AI, with a runtime environment for serving them.
gotchas: Official repository (agno-agi org) opened; metadata and README confirm Apache-2.0
Formerly Phidata
Actively developed

name: AutoGen
description: Microsoft Research framework for creating multi-agent AI applications that can act autonomously or work alongside humans; layered design with a Core API (message passing, event-driven agents, distributed runtime) and AgentChat (group chats, two-agent patterns), plus no-code AutoGen Studio.
gotchas: Official repository opened; legal notices state code is MIT (LICENSE-CODE), docs/content are CC-BY-4.0
In maintenance mode as of 2026; Microsoft directs new users to the Microsoft Agent Framework
Magentic-One (a multi-agent team for web/code/file tasks) is implemented in this repo rather than standalone

name: CAMEL
description: Multi-agent framework supporting communicative agents, agent societies, role playing, task automation, code generation, communication, memory, and data generation/simulation.
gotchas: Official repository (camel-ai org) opened; repository metadata and README confirm Apache-2.0 license
Actively developed (~13k+ stars)

name: CrewAI
description: Framework for building collaborative AI agent crews with defined roles, goals, and memory; Crews handle role-based collaboration while event-driven Flows enable more controlled, deterministic workflows.
gotchas: Official repository confirms MIT license and documents both Crews and Flows
Very active project (~35k+ stars)
Official docs linked from the README: https://docs.crewai.com/

name: Google Agent Development Kit (ADK)
description: Google's open-source agent development kit; code-first framework for building single agents and multi-agent systems with composition primitives such as sequential, parallel, and loop workflow agents plus sub-agent delegation.
gotchas: Python SDK; TypeScript and Go SDKs exist separately

name: LangGraph
description: Stateful orchestration layer for LangChain agents; models agents as nodes in a graph with durable execution, persistence, and streaming, supporting supervisor, sub-agent, and hierarchical multi-agent patterns.
gotchas: Official LangChain documentation; official README carries an MIT badge
The core multi-agent orchestration primitive in the LangChain ecosystem

name: MetaGPT
description: Multi-agent framework implementing an SOP-driven 'software company' — role-based agents (product manager, architect, engineer, QA) collaborate to generate PRDs, designs, and code.
gotchas: Official repository (FoundationAgents org) confirmed MIT in repository search results
One of the pioneering role-based multi-agent frameworks

name: OpenAI Agents SDK
description: Lightweight open-source Python library for building agentic apps; multi-agent workflows are expressed through handoffs and agents-as-tools, with built-in tracing and guardrails.
gotchas: Official OpenAI repository opened; README describes it as a lightweight yet powerful framework for multi-agent workflows, MIT licensed
Supersedes the experimental OpenAI Swarm

name: PraisonAI
description: Production-oriented multi-agent framework with self-reflection and low-code orchestration of role-based agent crews.
gotchas: Official documentation site opened; MIT badge confirmed in the docs source
Main repo is mervinpraison/praisonaidocs (docs) with the framework under the PraisonAI org

name: Semantic Kernel

gotchas: Official Microsoft repository; README confirms MIT license and explicitly describes building and orchestrating multi-agent systems
Multi-language (Python, .NET, Java)

Repository topics include multi-agent, multi-agent-systems, agent-framework, and orchestration

MIT open-source framework; commercial platform with a free tier

Plans: Plus $29.99/mo, Pro $99.99/mo, Max $199.99/mo, Enterprise custom; $50 free credits, no card

gotchas: Free tier exists historically; current positioning is enterprise-led (custom pricing)
SOC 2 Type II, GDPR
Used by Canva, Autodesk, Confluent

gotchas: Commercial platform with MIT open-source runtime components (SmythOS SRE)
Deploy via APIs, webhooks, scheduled agents, chat widgets

Region-limited (Bedrock Agents availability varies by AWS region)
Supervisor must be saved before collaborators can be attached

description: Stateful agents on Cloudflare Workers (Durable Objects) that can call and coordinate other agents via getAgentByName; official examples include multi-agent workers/pipeline patterns.

Multi-agent patterns documented in the official cloudflare/agents examples repo

description: Managed agent platform on Databricks: build multi-agent systems with a Supervisor Agent that orchestrates Genie Agents, agent endpoints, Unity Catalog functions, MCP servers, and custom agents.

ResponsesAgent (MLflow 3) is the current authoring interface
Supervisor Agent and some features are in beta

description: Google's managed agent runtime (Vertex AI Agent Engine rebranded) for deploying ADK multi-agent orchestrations — sub_agents, AgentTool, and graph workflows — as a service.

name: IBM watsonx Orchestrate

Dedicated docs at ibm.com/docs/en/watsonx-orchestrate (403 for the VM egress, not a product issue)
SaaS on IBM Cloud and AWS Marketplace; Agent Connect integrates external-framework agents

name: Microsoft Copilot Studio — Multi-Agent (Connected Agents)
description: Low-code agent platform where an orchestrator agent uses generative orchestration to delegate to connected specialist agents (Copilot Studio, Foundry, Fabric Data, A2A external agents).
gotchas: Official Learn training module (based on the classic Copilot Studio experience; a new experience shipped in 2026)
Multi-agent capability is preview/maturing; overlaps with Foundry workflows

description: Managed multi-agent orchestration in Foundry: visual/YAML workflows (Sequential, Group chat, Human-in-the-loop) invoking multiple Foundry agents with variables, versioning, and tracing.
gotchas: Renamed from 'Azure AI Foundry' to 'Microsoft Foundry' (2026)

name: Oracle AI Data Platform Workbench
description: Visual canvas builder for multi-agent systems on OCI: a Supervisor Agent node orchestrates executor specialist agents (SQL, RAG, HTTP, MCP tools) with memory and state-isolation policies.
gotchas: Official docs.oracle.com 'Agent Creation' guide covers Multi-agent Systems and Supervisor Patterns
Backed by OCI Generative AI service models; related to (but a distinct, newer builder from) the OCI Generative AI Agents service

name: Salesforce Agentforce — Multi-Agent Orchestration
description: Primary agent routes tasks to a team of specialist secondary agents powered by the Atlas Reasoning Engine, with A2A support for third-party agents and built-in observability.
gotchas: Verified on the official Salesforce product page (marketing page rather than help docs)
GA as of Sept 2026

name: ServiceNow AI Agent Orchestrator
description: Orchestrator coordinates teams of ServiceNow AI agents via Chain-of-Thought + ReAct, with shared memory across agent teams, AI Agent Studio, AI Agent Fabric (MCP/A2A), and AI Control Tower governance.
gotchas: Verified on official ServiceNow-hosted 'ServiceNow AI Agent Well-Architected Review' whitepaper (April 2026)
Now Assist / AI Agents are licensed per ServiceNow instance; GA since the Zurich release

name: A2A (Agent2Agent Protocol)
description: Open protocol for peer-to-peer agent collaboration: agents publish an Agent Card at /.well-known/agent-card.json, then exchange tasks and messages over JSON-RPC 2.0, gRPC, or REST with SSE streaming and push notifications.
gotchas: Created by Google (Apr 2025), donated to the Linux Foundation / Agentic AI Foundation; v1.0.0 released 2026-03
IBM's ACP was merged into A2A (Aug 2025)
Complementary to MCP (agent-to-agent vs agent-to-tool)

name: ACP (Agent Communication Protocol)
description: REST-native OpenAPI-defined protocol for agent-to-agent invocation: Agent Manifest discovery (GET /agents), runs (POST /runs) with sync/SSE/async modes, MIME-typed multipart messages, and trajectory metadata.
gotchas: Launched by IBM Research Mar 2025; merged into A2A under the Linux Foundation (Aug 2025)
Reference repo i-am-bee/acp is archived — legacy/superseded, build on A2A instead

name: Agent Protocol
description: Tech-agnostic OpenAPI specification defining a common REST interface for interacting with AI agents: create tasks (POST /ap/v1/agent/tasks), execute steps, and download/upload artifacts.
gotchas: See the official source for current details.

name: AGNTCY / OASF
description: Cisco Outshift-initiated open collective (now Linux Foundation) building the 'Internet of Agents': OASF is a standardized schema for describing agent capabilities/identity/IO (modeled on OCSF), plus an Agent Directory, SLIM secure messaging, and identity specs.
gotchas: A stack of specs/SDKs rather than one wire protocol; positioned to complement A2A and MCP
Includes Agent Connect Protocol (ACP) for messaging and SLIM (MLS-based, quantum-safe) transports

name: Agora
description: Decentralized protocol for LLM-agent communication: agents default to natural language for rare exchanges, then negotiate and exchange self-generated protocol documents (hash-identified) to use efficient routines for frequent interactions.
gotchas: Originated from Oxford research; fully decentralized with no central registry; MIT-licensed per the official FAQ

name: AITP (Agent Interaction & Transaction Protocol)
description: NEAR AI's open protocol for cross-trust-boundary interaction: agents communicate over Chat Threads (largely compatible with the OpenAI Assistants/Threads format) with extensible Capabilities for structured exchanges like payments, forms, and generative UI.
gotchas: Spec in progress; official docs show v0.1.0 Draft
Reference implementation target is agents on the NEAR AI Hub

name: ANP (Agent Network Protocol)
description: Open protocol suite for the Agentic Web: did:wba decentralized identity, WNS human-readable handles, agent description and discovery documents, secure end-to-end messaging profiles, and application-layer protocols.
gotchas: Spec organized around the ANP 1.1 release line; the meta-protocol specification remains a draft
Governance is a small GitHub community; adoption is thin outside China

name: AP2 (Agent Payments Protocol)
description: Google's open protocol for agent payment authorization: agents carry cryptographically signed mandates (Intent/Checkout/Payment Mandates as SD-JWT verifiable credentials) so every party can prove a purchase was authorized and audit it later.
gotchas: An authorization/audit layer, not a settlement rail; v0.2.0 (Apr 2026), standardization continuing in FIDO Alliance working groups
Originally an A2A AgentCard extension in v0.1; agent-to-agent delegation is out of scope in the current spec

name: Coral Protocol
description: MCP-native multi-agent coordination platform: agents join shared sessions over MCP, collaborate via @mention-addressed threads, and can be listed in a registry with Solana-based micropayments to agent developers.
gotchas: More platform + coordination pattern than neutral standard; graph-based multi-agent architecture (Anemoi) rather than hierarchical orchestration

name: DIDComm
description: Hyperledger/Aries messaging layer for secure agent-to-agent communication: DID-based, end-to-end encrypted, asynchronous messages (transport-agnostic) with standard protocol sequences (DID exchange, credential issuance, present-proof) on top.
gotchas: Genuinely agent-oriented (Aries agents' messaging layer) but rooted in the self-sovereign-identity world; broader multi-agent ecosystem adoption is limited

name: Eclipse LMOS Protocol
description: Eclipse Foundation protocol built on W3C Web of Things architecture: JSON-LD agent/tool descriptions signed with W3C DIDs, metadata propagation and discovery, transport-agnostic communication (lmosprotocol subprotocol), and DID/OAuth2 security schemes.
gotchas: Protocol text still work-in-progress (v1 namespace published); team signals intent to pursue W3C standardization
Eclipse project (EPL-typical licensing for Eclipse code, unverified)

name: FIPA-ACL / KQML
description: The original agent communication languages: KQML (DARPA, 1993) and FIPA-ACL (ratified 2000) standardized speech-act performatives (inform, request, propose, cfp) and interaction protocols like contract-net and subscribe/notify.
gotchas: Historic/legacy: formal semantics and ontology overhead limited adoption; FIPA became an IEEE Computer Society committee in 2005

name: MCP (Model Context Protocol)
description: Open standard (Anthropic, now under the Agentic AI Foundation) that standardizes how LLM applications connect to external tools, data sources, and prompts via JSON-RPC 2.0 in a client-host-server model.
gotchas: Current spec revision 2026-07-28 (stateless redesign)

name: NANDA
description: MIT Media Lab research infrastructure for the 'Internet of AI Agents': the NANDA Index (federated agent registry/name resolution), AgentFacts (capability documents signed as W3C Verifiable Credentials), and KYA third-party attestation.
gotchas: Discovery and trust layer, not a messaging wire protocol — it sits above MCP and A2A and does protocol translation via the NANDA Adapter

name: Activepieces
description: Open-source (Community Edition MIT) visual AI-automation platform: native AI pieces incl. a 'Run Agent' action that reasons through multi-step tasks with tools, human-in-the-loop approval pieces, and 280+ pieces published as MCP servers usable directly by LLMs in Claude Desktop/Cursor/Windsurf.
gotchas: Community Edition is MIT; packages/ee/ (enterprise features) are under a separate Commercial License
Like n8n, more automation-platform than durable agent infra — included on the strength of the Run Agent action + MCP toolkit

name: Camunda
description: Enterprise process-orchestration platform (Zeebe engine) that added native agentic capabilities: GA'd AI Agent connector (8.8, Oct 2025) with ad-hoc sub-processes where the LLM dynamically picks BPMN activities, A2A client connectors, built-in MCP server, and ProcessOS agent intelligence layer (beta).
gotchas: Enterprise BPMN platform — heaviest fit in this list; engine is source-available under the Camunda License v1 (production requires Enterprise license), not OSS

name: DBOS
description: Durable-execution library (Python/TypeScript/Go/Java) backed by Postgres: wrap any agent in DBOS workflows to checkpoint every LLM call and tool execution; first-party integrations for Vercel AI SDK (durableCalls middleware), OpenAI Agents SDK (DBOSRunner), Google ADK, and Pydantic AI.
gotchas: MIT across dbos-transact SDK repos
Lightweight approach: no separate orchestration cluster — durability lives in your app + Postgres
Official docs have a dedicated AI section (durable agents, parallelizing/scaling agents, HITL)

name: Hatchet
description: Distributed, fault-tolerant task queue and DAG workflow engine backed by Postgres: named 'AI agents' as an official use case — define agentic workflows as code, retry failures, parallelize agent actions, with fair queuing, rate limits, durable sleeps/event waits, and OpenTelemetry.
gotchas: Fully MIT licensed end-to-end; self-hosted or Hatchet Cloud
Younger project (0.x as of Sept 2026, ~7.9k stars) with fewer production war stories than Temporal; load-tested to ~10k tasks/s

name: Inngest
description: Event-driven durable-execution platform for TypeScript/Python/Go: write step functions (step.run/step.invoke/step.sendEvent) that look like normal code while Inngest handles retries, state, sleeps and event waits; first-class agent patterns (sync/async/scheduled sub-agent delegation) and durable AI-agent primitives.
gotchas: Self-hostable since Jan 2026, but licensed under SSPL (not OSI open-source)
Agent angle documented in Inngest's own blog ('durable AI agents', agentic patterns)
Best DX of the durable-execution class; lighter-weight than Temporal

name: LangSmith Deployment
description: LangChain's managed deployment for LangGraph multi-agent applications (renamed from LangGraph Platform, Oct 2025); the framework itself stays MIT open source.
gotchas: Renamed from LangGraph Platform to LangSmith Deployment in Oct 2025
Not full durable execution like Temporal — checkpointing + replay only

name: n8n
description: Fair-code visual workflow automation platform with mature AI capabilities: LangChain-based AI Agent nodes (Chat Trigger → AI Agent → chat model + memory + tools), human approvals, 1500+ integrations; self-hostable or n8n Cloud.
gotchas: Source-available under the Sustainable Use License (fair-code, not OSI open-source)
More 'AI workflow automation' than durable multi-agent infra — no event-replay durability; HITL is webhook/Wait-node based
Included because its AI Agent nodes are real and widely used for agentic automation

name: Orkes Conductor
description: Open-source (Apache 2.0) event-driven agentic workflow engine, originally Netflix Conductor and maintained by Orkes: durable execution with native LLM task types (14+ providers), MCP tool calling, vector DB support for RAG, and human approval gates; scales to billions of executions.
gotchas: OSS engine (github.com/conductor-oss/conductor) + Orkes SaaS enterprise offering
Agent features are native task types (not bolt-on)
Polyglot workers (Java/Python/Go/JS/C#/Ruby/Rust)

name: Prefect
description: Python-native workflow orchestration (@flow/@task decorators, retries, caching, scheduling): widely used as the orchestration layer under AI agents and agentic coding pipelines — durable per-agent runs with task-level observability, often paired with frameworks like Pydantic AI.
gotchas: Core engine Apache-2.0 (note: /server directory is under the Prefect Community License)

name: Restack
description: Enterprise AI agent platform and backend framework for building and deploying reliable AI agents: durable workflow orchestration, long-running agent execution, auto-generated REST APIs per agent/workflow, MCP tool exposure, Python/TypeScript SDKs on Kubernetes.
gotchas: Proprietary platform (enterprise tier); orchestration layer is built on Temporal under the hood
Primarily commercial — open-source examples and SDKs, but the core platform is not OSS

name: Restate
description: Open durable-execution foundation (Rust runtime + TS/Java/Python/Go/Kotlin SDKs) for building resilient agents: journals every step for crash recovery, durable promises for human-in-the-loop approvals, rollback/saga patterns for agents, and durableCalls middleware for Vercel AI SDK / LangChain / Pydantic AI.
gotchas: Runtime is BSL 1.1 source-available (not OSI open-source); SDKs are MIT
Dedicated AI docs (durable agents, HITL approvals, rollbacks)
Runs as a server in front of your agent service — similar footprint to a message broker

name: Temporal
description: Open-source durable-execution workflow engine (workflows/activities/signals); a first-class runtime for long-running multi-agent systems — official OpenAI Agents SDK integration (temporalio.contrib.openai_agents), framework-agnostic multi-agent fleets (Google ADK + LangGraph on Temporal), and durable human-in-the-loop signals.
gotchas: Server is MIT (Go); SDKs vary
Agent integration evidence: official temporalio/sdk-python openai_agents plugin and Temporal's Aug 2026 multi-agent blog
Known pitfall from docs: separate task queues for slow LLM inference vs other activities to avoid starvation

name: Trigger.dev
description: Open-source (Apache 2.0) developer platform for building AI agents and long-running durable workflows in TypeScript: no timeouts, durable checkpointing, automatic retries, queues/concurrency, human-in-the-loop waitpoints, tool calling/MCP support, and an MCP server for AI coding assistants.
gotchas: Originally a background-jobs framework (HN 2023); relaunched v3 in Sep 2025 with explicit AI-agent focus (YC W23, ~15.2k stars)
Self-hostable via Docker Compose/Kubernetes or managed cloud

name: Windmill
description: Open-source developer platform/workflow engine that turns scripts (Python, TS, Go, Bash, SQL...) into workflows, webhooks and UIs: DAG flows with branching, retries, approval steps (human-in-the-loop), and a built-in MCP server that exposes workflows to AI agents.
gotchas: AGPLv3 core (copyleft — check implications for hosted use; some modules Apache-2.0)
~16k stars
Strong fit for script-centric agent tool execution, approval gates, and agent-triggered flows via MCP

name: AgentLite
description: Salesforce AI Research's lightweight library for building task-oriented LLM agents and experimenting with reasoning strategies and multi-agent architectures.
gotchas: Paper + repo (SalesforceAIResearch/AgentLite); using arXiv URL

name: AgentVerse
description: Multi-agent framework that dynamically recruits and adjusts agent team composition during task-solving, and studies emergent positive/negative social behaviors of agent groups (ICLR 2024).
gotchas: Paper + repo (OpenBMB/AgentVerse); using arXiv URL

name: AutoAgents
description: Automatically generates and coordinates a team of specialized agents adapted to the task at hand, with an observer role reflecting on plans and agent responses to improve coherence.
gotchas: Paper + repo (Link-AGI/AutoAgents); using arXiv URL

name: AutoGen (paper)
description: Microsoft framework for building LLM applications through multi-agent conversation: 'conversable agents' combine LLMs, tools, and human input orchestrated via conversation programming.
gotchas: Paper + repo (microsoft/autogen); using arXiv URL

name: CAMEL: Communicative Agents
description: Role-playing framework where two LLM agents (AI User and AI Assistant) autonomously cooperate via 'inception prompting' to complete complex tasks; foundational work on communicative agents (NeurIPS 2023).
gotchas: Paper + open-source repo (camel-ai/camel, Apache 2.0 for code); using arXiv URL

name: ChatDev
description: Virtual software company: role-playing agents (CEO, CTO, programmer, reviewer, tester) collaborate through a 'chat chain' with communicative dehallucination to build complete software (ACL 2024).
gotchas: Paper + repo (OpenBMB/ChatDev, Apache 2.0 code / CC BY-NC 4.0 data); using arXiv URL

name: DyLAN
description: Dynamic LLM-agent network: automatically selects an agent team from a candidate pool and deactivates underperforming agents mid-task via an LLM ranker, with early stopping for efficiency.
gotchas: Paper + repo (SALT-NLP/DyLAN); using arXiv URL

name: Generative Agents
description: Stanford 'Smallville' simulation: 25 memory-enabled LLM agents exhibit believable emergent social behavior (information diffusion, relationship formation) in a sandbox world (UIST 2023).
gotchas: A social simulation rather than a workflow framework; included for its multi-agent social-behavior relevance and influence on later multi-agent simulation work

name: Magentic-One
description: Microsoft Research's generalist multi-agent system: a lead Orchestrator plans, delegates to specialist agents (web browsing, file handling, coding), and recovers from errors across GAIA, AssistantBench, and WebArena.
gotchas: Research system with open-source implementation in microsoft/autogen; using arXiv URL

name: MetaAgents
description: Collaborative generative agents with human-like reasoning and specialized skills coordinate in a simulated job-fair environment to study team formation and task-oriented multi-agent coordination.
gotchas: Latest arXiv revision (2025) retitles it 'MetaAgents: Large Language Model Based Agents for Decision-Making on Teaming'; same paper, same ID

name: MetaGPT (paper)
description: Encodes human Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) into multi-agent collaboration: specialized roles exchange structured artifacts via a shared message pool to build software (ICLR 2024 oral).
gotchas: Paper + repo (geekan/FoundationAgents MetaGPT, MIT); using arXiv URL

name: Multiagent Debate
description: Multiple LLM instances independently propose answers, then debate their reasoning over several rounds to converge on a more factual and better-reasoned final answer (ICML 2024).
gotchas: Founding paper of the multi-agent-debate sub-literature; the 'MultiAgent Debate (Du et al.)' entry merged here

name: AucArena
description: Evaluation suite simulating auctions where LLM bidding agents compete under budgets, benchmarking strategic planning and execution (budget management, goal adherence, adaptive strategy) in dynamic competitive multi-agent scenarios.
gotchas: Official suite name is 'AucArena' (paper: 'Put Your Money Where Your Mouth Is...'); third-party lists call it 'AuctionArena'

name: BattleAgentBench
description: Turn-based Battle City wargame benchmark with 7 sub-stages across 3 difficulty tiers that separately assess single-agent navigation, paired-agent task execution, and full multi-agent (2-team, 4-team, 8-agent) cooperation and competition.
gotchas: Tsinghua KEG, arXiv 2024; Level 1 is single-agent — multi-agent relevance is Levels 2–3

name: Collab-Overcooked
description: Two LLM agents cooperate via natural language in an extended Overcooked-AI kitchen across 30 open-ended tasks at 6 complexity levels, evaluated with process-oriented collaboration metrics (initiate vs. respond, trajectory efficiency).
gotchas: EMNLP 2025 Main; collaboration-focused (not competitive); open-source code at the repo linked in the paper

name: GameEval
description: Goal-driven conversational games (Ask-Guess, SpyFall, TofuKingdom) where LLM players take distinct roles with cooperative or adversarial objectives, probing cooperative/adversarial strategy, deception, multi-hop reasoning, and long-term planning.
gotchas: Code on GitHub is a third-party mirror (jordddan/gameeval); the paper's official code was released anonymously; license not confirmed

name: LLM-Coordination (LLM-Co)
description: Pure-coordination multi-agent benchmark: LLM agents act as proactive participants in four coordination games (Agentic Coordination), plus 198 multiple-choice CoordQA questions testing environment comprehension, Theory-of-Mind reasoning, and joint planning.
gotchas: UCSC, arXiv 2023 (v3 2025); code at github.com/eric-ai-lab/llm_coordination per the paper (license not confirmed)

name: MindAgent
description: Gaming-interaction infrastructure for multi-agent planning and coordination, with the CUISINEWORLD benchmark dispatching an LLM coordinator and multiple agents to play simultaneously, scored by the CoS (collaboration efficiency) auto-metric.
gotchas: NAACL 2024 Findings; also covers human-NPC collaboration; code at github.com/mindagent/mindagent (license not confirmed)

name: MultiAgentBench
description: Multi-agent-native benchmark on the MARBLE (Multi-Agent Coordination Backbone with LLM Engine) framework spanning 6 domains — research proposals, Minecraft building, coding, database error analysis (collaborative) plus Werewolf and bargaining (competitive) — with milestone-based KPIs comparing coordination topologies (star/chain/tree/graph).
gotchas: ACL 2025 (arXiv:2503.01935); original repo ulab-uiuc/MARBLE, also mirrored at MultiagentBench/MARBLE; repo license not confirmed

name: SOTopia
description: Open-ended social-interaction environment where LLM agents role-play characters with private goals across 90 social scenarios (negotiation, collaboration, competition), scored on goal completion and 7 social dimensions via SOTopia-Eval.
gotchas: ICLR 2024 spotlight; dyadic by default, SOTopia-S4 extends to multi-party; requires LLM API key + Redis to run

name: AgentMail
description: Email infrastructure built specifically for AI agents: programmatic inboxes (thousands of unique addresses via API), full send/receive, native threading, allowlists/blocklists, webhooks + WebSockets for event-driven agent communication.
gotchas: Commercial hosted product (official site agentmail.to; free tier with 3 inboxes)
Coordination angle: gives each agent its own identity for async two-way messaging

name: Cognee
description: Open-source memory control plane for agents: an Extract-Cognify-Load pipeline builds a self-hosted typed knowledge graph (Kuzu/LanceDB/SQLite) plus vector + relational stores so agents share persistent long-term memory across sessions.
gotchas: Apache-2.0
Emphasizes cross-agent knowledge sharing, tenant isolation, traceability/audit; ~30k stars
Commercial Cognee Cloud tier exists

name: Graphiti
description: Zep's open-source temporal knowledge-graph engine for AI agents: incrementally builds bi-temporal entity/fact graphs (Neo4j, FalkorDB, Neptune) with hybrid semantic + BM25 + graph-traversal retrieval, no LLM calls at query time.
gotchas: See the official source for current details.

name: LangGraph Checkpointing
description: Built-in state persistence for LangGraph agent workflows: a checkpointer snapshots full graph state after every super-step into threads (SQLite, Postgres, Redis, MongoDB), enabling pause/resume, time-travel debugging, and human-in-the-loop.
gotchas: Not a standalone repo — a LangGraph feature (LangGraph itself is MIT)
Companion BaseStore provides cross-thread shared memory (PostgreSQL/Redis/in-memory) used by LangMem

name: LangMem
description: LangChain's official long-term memory SDK for LangGraph agents: extracts and consolidates semantic, episodic, and procedural memories (incl. self-improving system-prompt optimization) backed by LangGraph's BaseStore.
gotchas: MIT
Extraction/consolidation layer over LangGraph storage, not a standalone DB; namespace isolation for multi-tenant memory; agent-facing manage/search memory tools

name: Letta
description: Platform for stateful AI agents with self-improving memory (formerly MemGPT, from the UC Berkeley research project): OS-inspired hierarchical memory (core blocks + archival recall) so agents persist and compound knowledge across sessions.
gotchas: Apache-2.0 confirmed via GitHub repo metadata

name: Mem0
description: Universal memory layer for AI agents: extracts facts from conversations into user/agent/session-scoped long-term memory with hybrid semantic + keyword + entity retrieval; the standard drop-in memory API for multi-agent apps.
gotchas: Apache-2.0 OSS repo plus managed Mem0 Platform (commercial)
Self-hostable with 20+ vector-store backends; optional graph backends (Neo4j, Memgraph, Kuzu)

name: Redis Agent Memory
description: Redis's managed memory layer for AI agents (part of Redis Iris, their real-time context engine): two-tier model with session memory (configurable TTL) and background promotion of extracted facts to long-term vector-backed memory.
gotchas: Apache License 2.0 per official README on the repo (opened 2026-09-29)
Repo is the research/open foundation; the production distribution is Redis Agent Memory in Iris via Redis Cloud
Ships MCP server interface

name: SuperMemory
description: Memory and context engine + API for the AI era: embeddings-based hybrid RAG + fact memory + evolving user profiles, with a hosted platform and a self-hostable local binary.
gotchas: MIT (repo LICENSE)
Cloud-first with self-host local binary; official plugins for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw + MCP server at mcp.supermemory.ai/mcp
Note: v0.0.7+ release notes mention a 10,000-document cap on self-hosted ('supermemory lite')

name: Zep
description: Commercial agent-memory platform that stores agent memory as temporal knowledge graphs — facts carry validity intervals so agents track what was true vs. what is true now.
gotchas: Managed product (Zep Cloud) is commercial/closed; open-source Community Edition deprecated April 2025 in favor of Graphiti
Treat acquisition claim as unconfirmed

name: 5dive
description: A company of AI agents on a server you own. You text them like coworkers.
gotchas: free and open source to self-host. Managed servers are paid, with a free trial.
